distinguishing_features: Embeds a porous metallic foam wick inside the bond coat to act as a lateral heat spreader at the TBC/BC interface
Reduces peak interfacial temperature by lateral thermal redistribution rather than adding insulation or stabilization
Uses an in-layer high-conductivity path within the coating stack itself rather than external cooling or operational changes
Operates on the oxidation-kinetics/CTE-stress driving variables via Arrhenius temperature reduction at the interface
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce peak interfacial temperature at the TBC/bond-coat interface during transient thermal cycling so as to lower bond-coat oxidation rate and CTE-mismatch thermal strain, thereby suppressing spallation.
parsed.viable_reason: A porous metallic foam embedded at the TBC/bond-coat interface with k~50 W/mK is itself oxide-forming, oxidation-prone, and thermally mismatched, and its supposed 70 K peak-temperature reduction rests on an unverified FEM assumption rather than a demonstrated lateral spreading path of meaningful capacity.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Embedding a lateral heat-spreader foam wick into the bond coat to flatten interfacial temperature peaks is not a routine parameter tweak of any of the cited monitoring, duty-cycle, or setpoint-cap arts and is inventive in concept, even though its physical feasibility is unproven.
